metadata.name: IdamBox CSRM Role, Function and FunctionApi Catalogue

designNotes: Functions are created once per unique menuPath. Dashboard:Dashboard and Risk Assessment Requests:Request Details are shared by both roles because those exact menu paths appear for both roles.

Questionnaire:Questionnaire Details and Questionnaires:Questionnaire Details are separate Function records because the source document uses different menu groupings for Requestor and Security Analyst.

Risk Register mitigation-control screens use CsrmControlImplementation because this entity represents a control contextualized for a particular CsrmRisk. Administration control screens use CsrmControl because it represents the reusable control catalogue.
API paths are proposed application APIs inferred from the UI functions and JDL model; they are not existing endpoints declared by the JDL.

The JDL does not currently contain an explicit assessment release flag or release date. The proposed release endpoint requires either a new field/state or a separate publication record to enforce Requestor read-only visibility after release.

The JDL does not contain persisted Alert, ReportDefinition, Attachment, Comment, or Activity/Audit entities. The proposed report and alert endpoints may initially be computed services; persisted workflow collaboration, file uploads, alerts, and audit history require model extensions.

Phase 3 serves only the eight questionnaire workflow operations represented in the authoritative OpenAPI contract. Review-comment, complete-review, and assessment-generation FunctionApi entries remain future catalogue intents and are not Phase 3 served routes.

Phase 7 serves GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary, GET /api/v1/alerts, GET /api/v1/alerts/summary, GET /api/v1/reports and GET /api/v1/reports/{reportKey} through five human Security Analyst-only API Functions, computed on read from existing records; their reserved FunctionApi entries moved from the Dashboard, Reports and Alerts menu Functions with their names, URLs and descriptions unchanged. GET /api/v1/dashboard/reports and GET /api/v1/dashboard/alerts stay unserved because the dedicated report and alert operations serve them. GET /api/v1/alerts/{alertId} stays unserved because a derived alert links straight to its source record. PATCH /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/acknowledge stays unserved because acknowledgement needs persisted per-analyst state, a datamodel change deferred beyond this milestone. POST /api/v1/reports/{reportKey}/export stays unserved because report export is deferred beyond this milestone. GET /api/v1/my_requests/status_summary is served as reserved, under the Requestor's My Requests Function.

Phase 8 records every catalogued FunctionApi no router serves in docs/references/served-operations.json with its reason, regenerated from the mounted Strapi by the served-operations test and read by the web chain guard: the five Phase 7 D-06 entries of note 8; the review-comment and complete-review intents of note 7 and the Phase 4 approve, submit_for_approval, regenerate_draft and due_for_review intents, superseded by the served release triple, the draft jobs and the analyst review list; the /api/v1 request aliases (my_requests, assessment_requests create, get, patch and submit, form_metadata, overdue, status_summary and the per-request information_systems and information_assets reads and writes), served through the core /api/csrm-assessment-requests routes, the /api/v1/information_* selectors and GET /api/v1/my_requests/status_summary; the control_implementations collection, detail, overdue and status_summary intents, served under their Risk; and the Risk export and close intents, deferred beyond this milestone, with the Risk overdue and status_summary intents superseded by the Phase 7 alerts and dashboard. The IAM content types (application, function, function-api, idambox-user and role) and the generic GET /api/csrm-information-systems and GET /api/csrm-information-assets reads are administered by IdamBox and unmounted from this API surface (D-36, D-44); their grants and OpenAPI entries stay for traceability, the served /api/v1/information_* selectors are the only reference-data read surface, and GET /api/applications is an intentionally unserved OpenAPI operation with no caller. Users & Permissions registration is disabled at bootstrap, while POST /api/auth/local and GET /api/users/me remain plugin routes recorded as an accepted residual until INT-02 (D-37).

roles.name: Security Analyst
roles.description: Reviews and manages cyber risk assessment requests and questionnaires; creates, edits, approves, and releases risk assessments; manages the risk register, mitigation control implementations, risk and control catalogues, reports, and alerts.

roles.name: Security Analyst Agent
roles.description: Automation agent with the same CSRM Function grants as the Security Analyst role.

roles.name: Requestor
roles.description: Creates and submits cyber risk assessment requests, collaborates on request details, completes assigned questionnaires, and views risk assessments after they have been released by a Security Analyst.

functions.name: My Requests

functions.name: New Request

functions.name: Request Details

functions.name: Questionnaires

functions.name: Risk Register

functions.name: Risk Details

functions.name: Risk Type Details

functions.name: Controls

functions.name: Information Systems

functions.name: Information System Details

functions.name: Information Assets

functions.name: Information Asset Details

functions.name: Reports
functions.description: Provides aggregated reporting over requests, questionnaires, assessments, risks, owners, treatments, and mitigation controls.

functions.name: Alerts
functions.description: Shows operational and risk alerts derived from overdue work, high residual risk, ineffective controls, and upcoming treatment or review dates.

functions.name: Current User Access API
functions.description: Server-side read grant for the signed-in IdamBox User's own effective access: display name, the menu Functions and the FunctionApi operations Strapi grants through Role -> Function -> FunctionApi. The web derives its navigation and capability checks from it; it never widens what the authorization policy allows. This API-only Function intentionally has no menuPath.
